Module Title: Electricity, Safety, Ohm’s Law, and Power
CETa Foundation / Activation: Voltage, current, resistance, power, polarity, reference, open/short circuit, and Week 1 safety boundaries.
Career Prerequisite Activation: Use only the Week 1 CETa electrical-quantity and safety foundation. No prior bench-equipment experience is assumed.
New Career Learning: Bench power supply, DMM modes/jacks, current limiting, pre-power inspection, first-power sequence, stop conditions, and hazard logging.
Genuine CETa/Career Overlap: CETa explains the electrical quantities; Career turns them into a controlled first-power and measurement workflow.
Future Preparation: Creates the bench habits required for every later measurement, bring-up, troubleshooting, and lab task.
Curriculum Source Basis: Georgia Piedmont Technical College — Electronics Technology — current catalog; Portland Community College — EET 101A — Electronic Lab and Essential Work Skills; Fluke — Digital Multimeter Basics; Fluke — Electrical Measurement Safety; NASA — NASA-HDBK-8739.21 — ESD Control

Module Title: DC Networks, Kirchhoff’s Laws, and Voltage Dividers
CETa Foundation / Activation: Series/parallel networks, KVL/KCL, dividers, expected node values, and reference-node reasoning.
Career Prerequisite Activation: Bring forward Week 1 safe measurement habits plus the Week 2 CETa network equations and expected-node reasoning.
New Career Learning: Expected-versus-actual troubleshooting, node tables, first hypotheses, divide-and-conquer test-point selection, and one-change-at-a-time discipline.
Genuine CETa/Career Overlap: Career uses the exact CETa node-voltage/current predictions as the known-good baseline for troubleshooting.
Future Preparation: Prepares the learner to choose instruments and high-information measurements rather than probe randomly.
Curriculum Source Basis: Georgia Piedmont Technical College — Electronics Technology — current catalog; Portland Community College — EET 101B — Electronic Equipment and Lab Skills; O*NET OnLine / U.S. Department of Labor — Electrical and Electronic Engineering Technologists and Technicians

New Career Learning: Question-first instrument selection, DMM/bench-supply/scope onboarding, probe/reference discipline, loading/accuracy/resolution, and reproducible evidence. Logic-analyzer use is deliberately deferred to Week 18.
Genuine CETa/Career Overlap: CETa supplies what electrical quantities and waveforms mean; Career teaches how a technician chooses and configures the instrument that can answer a specific question.
